Issues.Title: Fix ToolStripTextBox and ToolStripComBoBox in the toolbar do not scale well when bringing items down from 100% to 300%
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #8277, #5116


## Proposed changes

- Update hosted `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` controls to correctly synchronize their fonts when the parent `ToolStrip` DPI changes.
- Scale the hosted control width once using the old and new DPI values, and calculate the height from the preferred size after applying the correct font.
- Update the hosted control's `DeviceDpi` to prevent its font from being scaled more than once.
- Preserve custom fonts by scaling them once, while controls using the default font receive the new `ToolStrip` default font.
- Refresh the layout after applying the updated font and size.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` display an incorrect font and control size when an application moves between monitors with different DPI settings under Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness.
- After this change, the hosted text box and combo box correctly update their font, width, and height for the destination monitor.

## Regression? 

- Yes

## Risk

- Low. The change modifies DPI scaling behavior for hosted `ToolStrip` controls. The main risk is incorrect font or size scaling during repeated DPI transitions, especially for controls using custom fonts.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->

When moving the application between monitors with different DPI settings, `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` correctly update their font, width, and height to match the destination monitor.

Issues.Title: Clipboard reliability and EMF handling changes
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This change ports the Clipboard compatibility tests from .NET 9 to the current branch and restores behavior that regressed during the Clipboard and shared OLE refactoring.

It also hardens managed Clipboard ownership, transient native Clipboard reads, proxy behavior required by WPF, and native Enhanced Metafile (EMF) handling.

Existing typed Clipboard coverage is retained alongside the migrated legacy API tests.

## Issues addressed

### MTA Clipboard reads threw instead of returning neutral values

Clipboard read APIs had started throwing `ThreadStateException` on all MTA threads. In .NET 9, calls made from an MTA without a WinForms message loop returned API-specific neutral values such as:

- `null`
- `false`
- `string.Empty`
- Empty collections

This behavior is restored. MTA threads running a WinForms message loop continue to receive `ThreadStateException` because Clipboard access in that context requires STA.

### Argument validation occurred before the STA check

`Clipboard.SetDataObject` validated null arguments before validating the thread apartment, changing the observable exception type.

The .NET 9 exception precedence is restored:

- MTA with a null argument: `ThreadStateException`
- STA with a null argument: `ArgumentNullException`

### Typed text queries used unintended format conversion

Exact typed text queries could succeed because another text alias was available. Requests for `Text`, `UnicodeText`, or `System.String` now use exact-format lookup where required.

Case-insensitive fallback mappings such as `"TEXT"` to a canonical text format were also removed while preserving normal Windows format conversion behavior.

### Null custom-format values could not be stored

`Clipboard.SetData(format, null)` again supports null custom-format values. The implementation avoids the convenience `DataObject` constructor that rejects null before the data object can store it.

### Delayed-rendering Clipboard owners lost managed identity

`ClipboardCore` now retains the managed owner passed to `SetDataObject(copy: false)` and its exact COM identity through an `AgileComPointer<IDataObject>`.

WinForms can therefore return the original managed `IDataObject` while it remains the current Clipboard owner. Consumers such as WPF can continue requesting the OLE proxy to preserve Windows format-conversion behavior.

### Cached owners could become stale

A cached managed object is now validated with `OleIsCurrentClipboard` before it is returned.

The cache is discarded when:

- Another application or native caller replaces the Clipboard.
- The originating apartment has exited.
- The data is flushed with `copy: true`.
- The Clipboard is cleared.
- A subsequent object replaces the current owner.

Both proxy and unwrapped retrieval paths validate ownership, preventing a proxy read from leaving stale managed state behind.

### Exited STA owners could break later Clipboard operations

When a delayed-rendering owner STA exits, its Global Interface Table interface may no longer be retrievable.

The stale cache is now cleared and reads fall back to the current OLE Clipboard proxy. WinForms read APIs return neutral values without throwing, and another STA can subsequently replace or clear the Clipboard.

Cache replacement and cleanup are reentrancy-safe, and newly registered Global Interface Table cookies are not leaked if replacement fails.

### Global Interface Table revocation could assert after an STA exited

`AgileComPointer` now tolerates `E_INVALIDARG` when revoking a cookie whose source apartment has already exited.

Explicit disposal also suppresses finalization in a `finally` block so disposal tracking does not report a second failure after an explicit disposal attempt.

### Transient native Clipboard failures were not handled consistently

Native data-object operations can temporarily return `CLIPBRD_E_CANT_OPEN` even after `OleGetClipboard` succeeds.

A shared bounded retry policy is now applied to:

- HGLOBAL `QueryGetData`
- HGLOBAL `GetData`
- IStream `QueryGetData`
- IStream `GetData`
- Format-presence queries
- WinForms GDI bitmap `QueryGetData`
- WinForms GDI bitmap `GetData`

Only `CLIPBRD_E_CANT_OPEN` is retried. Permanent format, data, and medium errors continue to return immediately.

The GDI path ensures `Clipboard.GetImage()` receives the same transient-failure handling as text, audio, file-drop, custom-data, and typed reads.

### Native EMF media was not fully supported

The shared OLE adapters now support platform-opt-in native `TYMED_ENHMF` media.

The implementation:

- Advertises `TYMED_ENHMF` only when the platform supports it.
- Prefers native EMF when both `TYMED_ENHMF` and `TYMED_HGLOBAL` are requested.
- Falls back to HGLOBAL when native rendering fails and HGLOBAL is offered.
- Includes native media in `QueryGetData`, format enumeration, and native-to-managed probing.
- Rejects caller-provided EMF media in `GetDataHere`, where ownership cannot be transferred safely.
- Returns independently owned handles for repeated retrievals.
- Releases partially allocated native media when rendering fails.
- Releases retrieved media exactly once after conversion or type mismatch.

Native media support remains disabled by default and requires an explicit platform opt-in.

### Shared format mappings could not include platform-specific aliases

Shared mappings now combine common Clipboard aliases with optional platform-provided mappings. This allows consumers such as WPF to expose aliases required by their object model without causing WinForms to advertise unsupported formats.

## Test coverage

The migrated and expanded tests cover:

- Empty Clipboard behavior.
- STA and MTA access.
- MTA behavior with and without a WinForms message loop.
- Exception precedence and argument validation.
- Retry counts and delays.
- Delayed rendering and persistent Clipboard copies.
- Managed data-object identity.
- External owner replacement.
- Owners whose STA has exited.
- Proxy versus unwrapped reads.
- Exact text formats and Windows text conversion.
- Case-variant format names.
- Null custom-format values.
- Legacy `Clipboard.GetData` and `IDataObject.GetData`.
- Typed text, image, audio, file-drop, JSON, and custom data.
- Native-to-managed EMF conversion.
- Managed-to-native EMF rendering.
- Native EMF versus HGLOBAL medium selection.
- Native rendering fallback and handle cleanup.
- Repeated EMF retrieval and independent handle ownership.

EMF test infrastructure is separated into focused helper types:

- `EmfPayload`
- `EnhMetafileScope`
- `EmfNativeMethods`
- `EnhMetafileNativeDataObject`
- `EmfTestOleServices`

## Validation

- `System.Windows.Forms.Tests.ClipboardTests`: 206 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- Focused shared Clipboard/OLE tests: 82 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- Complete `System.Private.Windows.Core.Tests`: 892 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #10237


## Proposed changes

- Move the cached `_text` restoration using `PInvoke.SetWindowText(this, _text)` before `HandleHighDpi()` in `Control.OnHandleCreated`.
- Prevent the `FontChanged` event handler's updated `Text` value from being overwritten by stale pre-handle text.
- Add a regression test to validate hidden control font and text behavior during deferred handle creation under Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Hidden controls with an explicitly assigned font can receive an incorrectly scaled font when their handle is created under Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness.
- Text updated from a `FontChanged` event handler can display stale font information because the cached pre-handle text is restored after DPI handling.

## Regression? 

- Yes

## Risk

- Low. The change updates the ordering of cached text restoration and DPI handling in `Control.OnHandleCreated`. The main risk is a behavior change for controls that update their text during DPI-related font notifications.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cb593a6-2485-4fb6-86d9-272938c089bc

Issues.Title: Mouse-focused control displays focus border only after Tab navigation has been used
Issues.Body:
### .NET version

.NET 11 SDK: 11.0.100-rtm.26477.103

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Not tested/verified

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

No

### Issue description

The focus indicator behavior changes depending on whether keyboard navigation has previously been used.
When the application is first launched, clicking a control with the mouse gives the control focus, but no focus indicator is displayed.
After using Tab to navigate between controls, clicking the same control with the mouse displays the focus indicator.

This behavior occurs in both VisualStylesMode.Net11 and Classic:
- In Net11, a rounded solid focus border is displayed, making the behavior more noticeable.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/748e7142-f109-4479-9a8f-933af0a5e352

- In Classic, the same behavior occurs with the traditional dotted focus rectangle.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce1cc0c8-dcaf-40b7-9388-a90711123d6a

### Steps to reproduce


1. Create a .NET WinForms application with two Button controls under VisualStylesMode: NET11.
2. Run the application.
3. Click the first Button with the mouse. 
- No focus border is displayed.
4. Press Tab to navigate between the Buttons.
5. Click the first Button again with the mouse. 
- A focus border is now displayed.

Issues.Title: Fix Anchored controls scale incorrectly on multi-monitor setup using HDPI PerMonitorV2
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #10958


## Proposed changes

- Update `ContainerControl.ScaleContainerForDpi` so the DPI-scaled font is calculated and published before `SetWindowPos`, without raising `OnFontChanged` prematurely.
- Keep the final `OnFontChanged` processing in a `LayoutTransaction` after the native bounds update so autoscaling and anchored layout observe the latest font and bounds.
- Preserve the previous `_isScaledByDpiChangedEvent` state across nested DPI scaling operations.
- Retain the `IsHandleCreated` guard before calling `SetWindowPos`.
- Add regression coverage for anchored layout, explicit and inherited fonts, multiple DPI transitions, and reentrant DPI scaling.
- Preserve the ordering requirements identified by #9004/#9112 while covering the related owner/dialog DPI behavior from #8946.


<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Anchored controls no longer receive incorrect bounds when a PerMonitorV2-aware WinForms application moves between monitors with different DPI values.
- Controls anchored to opposing edges maintain their expected size and position when the application moves from the primary monitor to a secondary monitor and back.
- Nested DPI processing observes the latest scaled font and preserves the final font, bounds, and anchored-child layout.
- Existing behavior is preserved for controls with explicit fonts and controls inheriting their font from a parent.

## Regression? 

- No known regression.

## Risk

- Low to moderate. The change affects DPI font scaling, native window positioning, nested DPI processing, and layout ordering. The implementation preserves the existing `IsHandleCreated` guard and restores the previous nested DPI state after scaling.
- The affected scenarios are covered by round-trip and reentrant regression tests, with additional validation required for the actual multi-monitor owner/dialog message path.


<!-- end TELL-MODE -->


## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before

- When the application is moved from the primary monitor to the secondary monitor and then back to the primary monitor, the anchored Button changes size incorrectly.
- Attach a screenshot showing the incorrectly scaled Button after returning to the primary monitor.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f357bd6f-9a2e-47e0-bbb3-eb522d1a5bed

### After

- The anchored Button maintains the expected size after moving the application between monitors with different scaling values.
- Attach a screenshot showing the correctly scaled Button after returning to the primary monitor.

Issues.Title: Fix issue 15213: Bitmap finalized during Image.Save(Stream, ImageFormat) leaks native GDI+ memory
Issues.Body: Fixes #15213 ## Root Cause When `Image.Save(Stream, ImageFormat)` executes the internal stream-saving path, the `Image` object is not guaranteed to remain alive during the call to the native `GdipSaveImageToStream` function. Under specific timing conditions, the JIT compiler or Garbage Collector (GC) may trigger finalization of the `Image` object prematurely, creating a race condition with the native save operation; this results in the failure to release—or the loss of—underlying GDI+ image resources, manifesting as a native memory leak (where significant memory remains unrecovered). ## Proposed changes Within `CoreImageExtensions.Save(this IImage image, Stream stream, ...)` of `System.Private.Windows.GdiPlus`, wrap `GdipSaveImageToStream` in a try/finally block and call `GC.KeepAlive(image)` in the finally block. ## Customer Impact The correction avoids abnormal native memory growth in `Save(Stream, ImageFormat)` under high-pressure/specific GC timings, reducing memory risks and potential stability issues in long-duration or batch image processing scenarios. The impact on existing behavioral compatibility is minimal (only extending object survival to the end of the method), and should not change functional results or introduce visible behavioral differences. ## Regression? - Yes ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Test methodology - Manual ## Test environment(s) - 11.0.0-rc.2.26509.113 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15254)

Issues.Title: Fix extra inner border on FixedSingle TextBox after reopening the designer
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #14761

## Root cause
In .NET 11 visual styles, TextBoxBase custom-draws its non-client border and removes the native `WS_BORDER` style.

When a TextBox with `BorderStyle.FixedSingle` was initially created using classic visual styles and later transitioned to VisualStylesMode.Net11, the existing native EDIT handle was updated in place. This did not reliably remove the native border state established during handle creation.

Consequently, the native inner border remained visible underneath the custom .NET 11 border, producing a double-border appearance after the WinForms Designer was closed and reopened.

## Proposed changes

- Update TextBoxBase.GetVisualStylesModeChangeImpact so that a TextBoxBase with BorderStyle.FixedSingle recreates its native handle when transitioning between classic and .NET 11 visual styles.

    Recreating the handle ensures that its CreateParams are applied from a clean state and that the native WS_BORDER style is not present in .NET 11 mode.


<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Customers using VisualStylesMode.Net11 with `BorderStyle.FixedSingle` TextBox controls no longer see an unexpected inner border after a debugging session or after reopening the WinForms Designer.

## Regression? 

- No

## Risk

- Minimal

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->


## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before
Create a form using VisualStylesMode.Net11, add a **TextBox** with `BorderStyle.FixedSingle`, Start and stop debugging or closed and reopen the WinForms Designer.  The TextBox can display both:  the expected .NET 11 outer border and an unexpected native inner border.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28ec9e37-f128-462e-8ca7-a64933babf0b


### After
A FixedSingle TextBox recreates its native handle when crossing the classic/.NET 11 visual-styles boundary. The stale native `WS_BORDER` state is removed. Only the expected .NET 11 border is rendered after reopening the Designer.
